business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward and forward integration within a single site cluster: the Company describes itself as an integrated iron and steel manufacturing company operating two integrated divisions - a Steel Melting Shop (SMS) and Foundry Division and a Rolling Mill Division. The SMS runs 12 MT fully digital medium-frequency induction furnaces in twin-shell configuration with secondary metallurgy via ladle refining furnace (LRF) and vacuum degassing (VD); the foundry has an in-house engineering and pattern development unit, continuous sand mixers, mechanised fettling via automatic shakeout, a sand reclamation plant, shot blasting and automatic paint booths; downstream are heat treatment furnaces, machine shops (>100,000 sq ft covered, CNC lathes, boring machines, roll grinding, VTL/CNC VTL, plano and CNC vertical milling) and rolling mills. Manufacturing and machining processes are described as overlapping and fungible, so the available (installed) capacity of the SMS and Foundry Division can vary with the product mix being run. Upstream, raw material (scrap, ingots, ferro alloys) is procured directly from domestic manufacturers and international suppliers without middlemen, on purchase orders rather than long term contracts; internally generated scrap is re-melted and recycled. Downstream, the Company sells directly through its in-house sales team, keeping middle-men and agents out of the sales process because products are highly customised and engineered; orders are purchase-order based with customer projections used for production planning, and long term contracts are generally avoided due to steel price volatility. Utilities: a 66 KvA sub-station, grid power from the Punjab State Electricity Board, ground water, and around 2 MW of installed rooftop solar. Corporate structure was consolidated through a Scheme of Amalgamation (NCLT Chandigarh order dated August 22, 2024) merging Belco Special Steels Private Limited (now the Rolling Mill Division) and Parkash Multimetals Private Limited (now part of the SMS and Foundry Division) into the Company.

governance.property_leased_from_promoter_group_note: The corporate office and all green-belt land adjoining the manufacturing site are held from promoter-family lessors, and all four arrangements expire on the same date — January 31, 2027, within months of the intended listing. Rent to these lessors appears in the RPT rows: Yogita Garg 19.2 ₹ lakh, Anju Garg 2.4 ₹ lakh and Aakanksha Garg 12.0 ₹ lakh in Fiscal 2026. Yogita Garg is also a Promoter Group Selling Shareholder in the Offer (up to 2,143,623 shares). The RHP nonetheless asserts there is 'no conflict of interest with lessors of our immovable property'.
record_gaps: Degree certificates and marksheets evidencing the educational qualifications of two Promoters who are also Directors — Parkash Chand Garg (Chairman) and Rajesh Garg (Vice Chairman) — are not traceable. Written applications to the relevant universities/colleges did not produce them, so the qualifications disclosed in 'Our Management' rest solely on affidavits furnished by these Promoters to the Company and the BRLMs, plus copies of correspondence with the university (Risk Factor 29).

Certain corporate records of the Company are untraceable: the Company relies on certificates dated August 5, 2026 from Chauhan Pradeep & Associates, practising Company Secretary, named as an 'expert' under Section 26(5) of the Companies Act specifically 'in connection with certain untraceable corporate records of our Company'. The RHP does not enumerate which records are missing, so the extent of the gap cannot be assessed from the filing.

Return of allotment (Form 2) for the September 12, 2011 allotment of 55,500 equity shares was filed with incorrect allottee names ('Anil Gupta Ind.' and 'Shentam Gupta' rather than 'Anil Gupta' and 'Shantum Gupta'); the correct names survive only in the register of members, so the RoC record and the Company's own record diverge.

Form 32 for Dinesh Garg's appointment as Whole Time Director in Fiscal 2010 recorded his category as 'Independent' — the RoC record of the founder-director's category is wrong on file and has not been rectified.

The shareholders' resolution and Form DIR-12 for Ayussh Mittaal's independent directorship record a non-existent term end date ('February 30, 2030'), corrected only by a later board note rather than by a fresh filing.

The financial performance of the sole Group Company, BLC Metals Private Limited — reserves, sales, profit after tax, EPS, diluted EPS and net asset value for Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 — is not printed in the RHP and is hosted only on the Company's website, so those figures are simply unavailable from the filing.

Inventory was not valued for the quarters ended June, September and December 2025 for the purpose of the stock statements filed with lenders ('Refer Note-1'), so no book-versus-return comparison exists for three of the four quarters of Fiscal 2026.
The RHP does not state the reason for the mid-term resignation of the erstwhile statutory auditor, M/s Bansal Jiwan & Associates, which created the casual vacancy filled on August 1, 2024.

No CARO 2020 annexure and no Rule 11(g) audit-trail reporting appears anywhere in the RHP; their absence from the filing means no adverse-remark position can be established either way from this document.
red_flags: Family control is close to total: 4 of the 10 directors plus the CEO, COO and CFO are all members of the Garg family (father, brothers, sons, grandsons), the Chairman's grandson holds the CFO post — the officer whose independence from management matters most for financial reporting — and the Managing Director sits on the Audit Committee that oversees him.

Three Promoter Group entities are in a similar line of business (BLC Metals Private Limited, Kunj Forgings Private Limited, Kanha Kunj Forge Private Limited) and two serving issuer directors sit on BLC Metals' board; the RHP concedes the common-pursuits conflict yet asserts in the same section that the Promoters have no interest in any similar venture, and states only that conflict procedures will be adopted 'as and when' a conflict arises.

The Company routed a ₹ 240.32 million (2,403.2 ₹ lakh) loan through BLC Metals in Fiscal 2024 — 5.39% of revenue from operations — repaid within the same year with ₹ 4.98 million of interest, and paid it a further ₹ 94.00 million on preference share redemption in Fiscal 2025.

Promoter and family funding of the balance sheet was pervasive and then abruptly unwound before the Offer: ₹ 218.51 million of loans accepted and ₹ 251.35 million repaid in Fiscal 2024, ₹ 1.81 million accepted and ₹ 331.73 million repaid in Fiscal 2025, spread across 15 individual family members and HUFs — and effectively nil in Fiscal 2026.

Promoters personally guarantee bank facilities sanctioned at ₹ 165.00 million (ICICI) and ₹ 675.79 million (HDFC); the Company's funding therefore depends on individuals, and the RHP itself warns that any failure to maintain those guarantees could accelerate the facilities.

The corporate office and all green-belt land are leased from promoter-family members (Yogita Garg, Anju Garg, Aakanksha Garg) on four arrangements that all expire on January 31, 2027, months after the intended listing, while the RHP asserts there is no lessor conflict of interest — and Yogita Garg is simultaneously selling up to 2,143,623 shares in the Offer.

The independent-director cohort and all five board committees were created on a single day (February 25, 2025) shortly before the DRHP; the same three Independent Directors staff every committee while the two most experienced steel-industry Independent Directors sit on none.

Quarterly stock and book-debt statements filed with HDFC and ICICI for drawing-power purposes diverge materially from the books — up to ₹ 80.23 million on book debts and ₹ 70.84 million on inventories — and inventory was simply not valued for three quarters of Fiscal 2026.

Delays in remitting statutory dues worsened rather than improved in the pre-IPO year: TDS delays rose to 17 instances and 2,566 aggregate days in Fiscal 2026 from 15 instances and 2,010 days in Fiscal 2025, with a first GST delay of 337 days in Fiscal 2026.

Record integrity is weak for a company incorporated in 1995: the Chairman's and Vice Chairman's educational documents are untraceable, an outside practising CS had to certify 'certain untraceable corporate records', and three RoC filings carry incorrect information — one of which records the Managing Director as an 'Independent' director.

The statutory auditor resigned mid-term in 2024 with no reason disclosed, and the successor firm — appointed on August 1, 2024 to fill the casual vacancy — signed the Fiscal 2024 audit report seven weeks later and now certifies all three restated years.

overview.business_model: The Company melts, casts, machines and rolls steel at two owned manufacturing facilities in Mandi Gobindgarh, Punjab (together approximately 790,000 sq ft, combined installed capacity of 119,690 MT comprising 54,690 MT of finished steel processing and 65,000 MT of rolling mill capacity) and sells four families of precision engineered products: metal rolls for rolling mills (alloy cast steel, adamite, graphitic steel, S.G. iron pearlitic and bainitic, indefinite chill and forged rolls), engineering castings of 500 kg to 20 MT per unit, alloy/carbon/stainless steel bars in sections from 6 mm to 230 mm, and forging ingots and forged shafts/blocks of 500 kg to 15 tons. Sales are made against customer purchase orders rather than long-term contracts (stated to be because of steel price volatility), which also lets the Company decide case-by-case whether to extend credit. End-user industries include steel, mining and aggregate crushers, power, sugar, automobile, infrastructure and construction, aerospace and defence and cement. In Fiscal 2026, revenue from operations was Rs 5,340.25 million, of which Alloy Steel Products contributed Rs 2,446.10 million (45.81%), Metal Rolls Rs 1,407.41 million (26.35%) and Engineering Castings Rs 1,043.39 million (19.54%); repeat customers contributed Rs 4,522.77 million (84.69%) and the top 10 customers Rs 2,029.21 million (38.00%). Total capacity utilisation was 87.71% in Fiscal 2026. A third (Upcoming) manufacturing facility at Village Salani, Tehsil Amloh, Mandi Gobindgarh, District Fatehgarh Sahib, Punjab is under construction.

genesis.founding_story: The RHP states the group traces back to 'Behari Lal & Sons', a steel commodities trading firm based in Mandi Gobindgarh, Punjab, which entered trading of steel billets, sponge iron/DRI and ferro alloys. Building on that trading base, BLEL was established in 1995 by its current Chairman and Promoter Parkash Chand Garg, described as having over 31 years of experience in the steel industry and as having been a director of the Company for 30 years. Growth was furthered by Rajesh Garg (Vice Chairman and Promoter, over 29 years of industry experience, 28 years as a director of the Company) and Dinesh Garg (Managing Director and Promoter, 30 years as a director). In February 2012 the Company started commercial production of steel products through its Steel Melting Shop and Foundry Division at Mandi Gobindgarh, converting it into a full-fledged manufacturing enterprise. Growth was further accelerated by the entry of the fourth generation, marked by Lovlish Garg (son of Rajesh Garg) joining the business; he has been on the Board since 2016. In March 2022 the group commissioned its Rolling Mill Division at Mandi Gobindgarh under Belco Special Steels Private Limited, since merged into the Company. Senior management includes Bhuvnesh Garg (CEO), Aakarsh Goyal (CFO) and Kanav Garg (COO).

litigation_summary.materiality_threshold: Materiality Policy adopted by the Board on September 8, 2025. Outstanding litigation/arbitration other than criminal, statutory/regulatory, SEBI-disciplinary and tax matters is 'material' if the aggregate monetary claim exceeds the LOWEST of: (i) 2% of turnover per the latest annual Restated Financial Statements = ₹ 106.81 million; (ii) 2% of net worth = ₹ 61.22 million; (iii) 5% of the average absolute value of profit or loss after tax for the last three years = ₹ 25.56 million — i.e. an effective threshold of ₹ 25.56 million (255.6 lakhs); or where liability is not quantifiable but the outcome may have a material adverse effect. Material creditors threshold: 5% of total trade payables = ₹ 10.09 million.

concerns_observed: The single hardest disclosure in the filing: the quarterly stock and book-debt statements filed with HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank for drawing-power purposes diverge materially from the books of account in EVERY quarter of all three fiscals. Year-end examples as printed (₹ million): inventories Mar-24 books 605.60 vs statement 595.59; Mar-25 810.98 vs 760.18; Mar-26 1,048.10 vs 977.26 (a ₹ 70.84 mn gap). Book debts Mar-24 813.39 vs 837.00; Mar-25 783.86 vs 824.53; Mar-26 958.06 vs 996.84; the largest single quarterly gap is Jun-24 book debts 801.42 vs 881.65 (₹ 80.23 mn). For the quarters ended June, September and December 2025 inventory was NOT VALUED AT ALL ('Refer Note-1'). Management's explanation is that inventory is valued only annually and that entries were pending posting, and that the banks accepted the returns without objection; the Company does not characterise this as a non-compliance.

ZERO of the ₹ 630.39 million capital expenditure is committed. The RHP states: 'As on the date of this Red Herring Prospectus, our Company has not made any payment towards funding the said Capital Expenditure' and 'We have not entered into any definitive agreements with any of these vendors and we cannot assure you that the same vendors would be engaged... or at the same costs.' No purchase order has been placed against any of the 38 quotation line items; vendors were only approved by a Board resolution dated June 28, 2026. Nine quotations carry 4-month validity from June 4–6, 2026 and therefore lapse around early October 2026 — among them the Adhvika ForgeTech 1600 T forging press (₹ 98.90 mn), the 7 ton charger manipulator (₹ 39.80 mn), the 2T hammer (₹ 28.70 mn), the 5 ton CNC forging manipulator (₹ 26.70 mn) and the Precitec double-column VMC (₹ 48.40 mn) — while 100% of every quantified object is scheduled for deployment in Fiscal 2027 and nil is deployed to date. No amount is summed here.

Neither the appraisal nor the monitoring safeguard applies. The RHP states 'None of the Objects of the Offer for which the Net Proceeds will be utilized have been appraised by any agency' and that the fund requirements 'have not been appraised by any bank, or financial institution'; and 'Since the Fresh Issue size does not exceed ₹ 1,000 million, our Company is not required to appoint a credit rating agency as the monitoring agency... in accordance with Regulation 41'. Oversight rests on quarterly disclosure to the Audit Committee — an Audit Committee on which the Managing Director sits.

The larger half of the capex buys no net capacity at Facility 1 and the added capacity at Facility 2 is not stated to be order-backed. Per the chartered engineer's certificate, Manufacturing Facility 1's installed capacity is expected to be UNCHANGED at 54,690 MT (metal rolls and engineering castings +5,000 MT offset by ingots −5,000 MT), while Facility 2 rises by 15,000 MT over its existing 65,000 MT. The RHP never states the added capacity is supported by existing orders — its stated rationale is 'In line with the growth in the industry and our strategies' — and no customer contract, LOI or offtake commitment is tied to it.

Utilisation FELL in the most recent year at the division being expanded, with no capacity added. Rolling Mill Division utilisation was 82.02% in FY26 against 88.24% in FY25 and 85.48% in FY24, on installed capacity flat at 65,000 MT in all three years; aggregate utilisation fell to 87.71% from 90.30%. Actual production fell to 104,980 MT from 107,879 MT. Only the SMS and Foundry Division rose, to 94.47%.

Working capital stretched sharply in the pre-Offer year and consumed the profit growth. On the RHP's own printed measure, working capital days rose to 132 in FY26 from 104 (FY25) and 98 (FY24), with net working capital of ₹ 1,924.50 / 1,453.68 / 1,196.40 mn; inventory days rose to 57 from 42 and 34, and the cash conversion cycle to 93 days from 72. Cash flow before working capital changes rose to ₹ 981.49 mn from ₹ 775.84 mn, but a ₹ (488.61) mn working-capital movement cut net cash from operating activities to ₹ 275.38 mn in FY26 from ₹ 618.86 mn in FY25. Cash and cash equivalents at March 31, 2026 were only ₹ 11.42 million.

Receivables past 90 days more than tripled: ₹ 167.55 million at March 31, 2026 against ₹ 46.91 mn (FY25) and ₹ 58.55 mn (FY24), while the allowance for expected credit loss stands at just ₹ 2.17 mn. Trade receivables are ₹ 957.74 mn or 17.93% of revenue; the RHP states no specific due dates are agreed on trade receivables, so ageing is prepared from the transaction date.

Family control is close to total across both the board and the finance function: 4 of 10 directors (Parkash Chand Garg, Rajesh Garg, Dinesh Garg, Lovlish Garg) plus the CEO (Bhuvnesh Garg), COO (Kanav Garg) and CFO (Aakarsh Goyal) are all Garg-family members, and the CFO is the Chairman's grandson. The Promoters and Promoter Group hold 34,553,485 Equity Shares or 88.51% of pre-Offer capital; the post-Offer percentage is printed as [●].

The committee architecture was assembled in a single day and concentrates on three people. All five board committees were constituted on February 25, 2025; the same three Independent Directors (Ayussh Mittaal, Meena Rohilla, Anil Kumar Bansal) staff every one of them, while Anil Dhawan and Rajesh Kumar Sinha — the two Independent Directors with roughly 36 and 22 years of steel-industry experience — sit on no committee at all. The Managing Director is a member of the Audit Committee and CHAIRS the Risk Management Committee. The RHP separately discloses that 4 of the 5 Independent Directors have never been independent directors of a listed company and that no non-independent director has served on a listed board.

The statutory auditor resigned mid-term on August 1, 2024 and the RHP gives NO reason. M/s Ashwani & Associates was appointed the same day to fill the casual vacancy and signed the audit report for the year ended March 31, 2024 seven weeks later, on September 27, 2024; the same firm now certifies all three restated years (examination report June 11, 2026, UDIN 26506955HXDAZV4293). Separately, NO CARO 2020 annexure and no Rule 11(g) audit-trail reporting appears anywhere in the RHP — an absence of disclosure, from which no adverse-remark position can be read either way.

Statutory-dues discipline WORSENED into the pre-IPO year rather than improving: TDS delays rose to 17 instances and 2,566 aggregate days in FY2026 from 15 instances and 2,010 days in FY2025 (nil in FY2024), and FY2026 carries a first GST delay of 1 instance and 337 days (₹ 0.41 mn). TCS was 1 instance / 117 days in FY2026 after 4 instances / 1,562 days in FY2025. All dues are stated to have been paid subsequently, with no action initiated.

The demand base is entirely short-cycle by the Company's own design. The RHP states 'We do not enter into long term contracts with our customers (i.e. contracts for a duration of more than 1 year) primarily due to volatility in the steel price', and the same absence applies upstream — no long-term contracts or arrangements with raw-material suppliers, only purchase orders. Annual customer churn rose to 38.58% in FY26 from 34.73% and 34.87%, with only 62.98% of prior-year customers retained and unique new customers of 144 / 138 / 157 across FY26 / FY25 / FY24.

The largest end-market shrank in absolute rupees, and so did the largest product line. Automobile revenue fell to ₹ 2,063.85 mn (38.65% of revenue) in FY26 from ₹ 2,475.88 mn (48.75%) and ₹ 2,480.73 mn (55.61%) — the RHP itself states 'our revenue from the automobile industry has reduced in absolute Rupee terms as well'. Alloy Steel Products, the largest product family, fell to ₹ 2,446.10 mn (45.81%) from ₹ 2,582.09 mn (50.84%), with sales volume of 35,185 t against 39,952 t.

Input cost dominates the P&L with no pass-through assurance and no supplier contracts: cost of materials consumed was 68.62% / 60.78% / 61.02% of total expenses across FY24–FY26 (₹ 2,745.21 / 2,716.46 / 2,806.58 mn), of which scrap steel alone is 46.10% of total expenses in FY26 (₹ 2,120.51 mn) and ingots 11.42%. Top-10 suppliers are 38.39% of total expenses and, measured against total purchases, 49.00%. The RHP states margins will be affected 'if, and to the extent, we are unable to pass on the price escalation'.

The corporate office and all three green-belt land parcels are leased from promoter-family members (Yogita Garg, Anju Garg, Aakanksha Garg) on 11-month arrangements that ALL expire on the same date, January 31, 2027 — within months of the intended listing, with renewal at the lessors' discretion. Yogita Garg is simultaneously a Promoter Group Selling Shareholder offering up to 2,143,623 Equity Shares. Three Promoter Group entities — BLC Metals Private Limited, Kunj Forgings Private Limited and Kanha Kunj Forge Private Limited — are in a similar line of business, and two serving issuer directors (Vice Chairman Rajesh Garg and Managing Director Dinesh Garg) sit on BLC Metals' board. BLC Metals is the sole Group Company and NO financials for it are printed in the RHP — reserves, sales, PAT, EPS and NAV are hosted only on the Company's website.

Corporate-record integrity is weak for a company incorporated in 1995: the degree certificates and marksheets of the Chairman (Parkash Chand Garg) and Vice Chairman (Rajesh Garg) are untraceable, so their disclosed qualifications rest on affidavits; an outside practising Company Secretary (Chauhan Pradeep & Associates) has been named an 'expert' under Section 26(5) specifically 'in connection with certain untraceable corporate records', without the RHP enumerating which records are missing; and three RoC filings carry incorrect information — Form 32 recording founder-Managing Director Dinesh Garg's category as 'Independent', a DIR-12/shareholder resolution recording an independent-director term ending on the non-existent date 'February 30, 2030', and a 2011 return of allotment naming 'Anil Gupta Ind.' and 'Shentam Gupta'.

The only third-party priced primary issuance in the recent build-up is the January 20, 2024 placement to Homedge Infracon (now SG Tech Engineering) at ₹ 448.26 per share.

Foreign-currency exposure is wholly unhedged while export revenue more than doubled: revenue denominated in foreign currency ₹ 393.65 mn (7.37% of revenue) in FY26 from ₹ 183.84 mn, with net exposure at March 31, 2026 of EUR 0.64 million (₹ 70.13 mn) and USD 0.04 million (₹ 4.03 mn). Unhedged foreign-currency exposure (EUR 0.64 mn and USD 0.04 mn at March 31, 2026) against export revenue that rose to ₹ 479.78 mn (8.98% of revenue), and the settled level of US reciprocal tariffs on Indian exports — 26% (April 2025) to 50% (August 2025) to an interim 18% (February 2026), still under negotiation.

open_questions: The quarterly stock and book-debt statements filed with HDFC and ICICI diverged from the books in every quarter of three fiscals, and inventory was not valued at all for the quarters ended June, September and December 2025 — what drawing power was actually availed against those returns, what did the banks say in writing when the divergences were disclosed to them, and what changes to the quarterly inventory-valuation process have been made for Fiscal 2027?

100% of the ₹ 630.39 mn capex rests on quotations, with nine of them (including the ₹ 98.90 mn forging press and ₹ 48.40 mn VMC) lapsing around early October 2026 — what happens to the cost estimate and the Fiscal 2027 schedule if those quotations expire before Allotment, and which of the 38 line items would be re-quoted or dropped?

The RHP nowhere states that the 15,000 MT addition at Facility 2 is backed by orders, while the Company signs no contract longer than one year — what customer commitments, if any, underpin the new forging line, and what utilisation is expected on it in Fiscal 2028?

Facility 1's spend produces no net capacity change (rolls and castings +5,000 MT, ingots −5,000 MT) — what is the expected realisation and margin per tonne on the substituted mix, and over what period is the ₹ 195.89 million of Facility 1 equipment and machinery spend expected to pay back?

Why did M/s Bansal Jiwan & Associates resign as statutory auditor mid-term on August 1, 2024, and what procedures did the successor firm perform to sign the Fiscal 2024 opinion seven weeks after being appointed to the casual vacancy?

No CARO 2020 annexure and no Rule 11(g) audit-trail reporting appears anywhere in the RHP — what do the CARO 2020 annexures and the Rule 11(g) paragraphs to the FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 standalone audit reports actually say, particularly on inventory verification, statutory dues and the accounting-software audit trail?

Working capital days rose to 132 from 98 and CFO fell to ₹ 275.38 mn on a ₹ (488.61) mn working-capital build, while over-90-day receivables tripled to ₹ 167.55 mn — which customers or product lines drove that build, and how much of it had unwound by the June and September 2026 quarters?

All four leases of the corporate office and green-belt land from Yogita Garg, Anju Garg and Aakanksha Garg expire on January 31, 2027 — on what terms and at what rent will they be renewed, and how is that negotiated at arm's length when one lessor is simultaneously selling up to 2,143,623 shares in this Offer?

BLC Metals Private Limited is a Group Company in a similar line of business with two issuer directors on its board, and its reserves, sales, PAT, EPS and NAV are hosted only on the Company's website rather than printed — what were its revenue and profit in Fiscals 2024, 2025 and 2026, and what business does it (and Kunj Forgings and Kanha Kunj Forge) do that the issuer does not?

The Promoters' build-up table records a gift of 2,190,000 Equity Shares (5.61% of pre-Offer capital) from Anju Garg to Lovlish Garg on September 18, 2025, yet the 'last 5 primary or secondary transactions' table lists only the May 19, 2025 gift of 2,614,740 shares and two one-share gifts of September 1, 2024 as secondary transactions — on what basis was the most recent and second-largest gift omitted from that table?

The RHP names a third indirect-tax proceeding inside the ₹ 8.04 million indirect-tax figure but itemises only two (the ₹ 6.98 mn CGST matter and the ₹ 0.66 mn show-cause notice) — what is the third matter, its forum and its status?

TDS delays rose to 17 instances and 2,566 aggregate days in Fiscal 2026 from 15 instances and 2,010 days in Fiscal 2025, with a first 337-day GST delay — what specifically failed in the compliance process in the year the Company was preparing to list, and what interest or penalty exposure remains?

The credit rating moved from CRISIL BBB+/A2 to CARE A-/A2+ on August 3, 2026 while the RHP describes the rating as having 'remained consistent' — why was the rating agency changed, and was a rating obtained from CRISIL for Fiscal 2026 before the switch?

The certificates of Chauhan Pradeep & Associates dated August 5, 2026 are relied on 'in connection with certain untraceable corporate records' without the RHP saying which records — which corporate records are missing, for what periods, and what was reconstructed from what evidence?

The 'Behari Lal' wordmark application in classes 6 and 7 is pending and objected — what is the ground of objection, what is the current status of the reply, and what is the plan if registration is refused for a mark that is the Company's own name?
verdict.our_read: A profitable, family-controlled steel and precision-components maker (FY26 revenue ₹ 5,340.25 mn, PAT ₹ 646.36 mn, D/E 0.06) whose Offer funds ₹ 630.39 mn of capex with zero orders placed, while its bank stock statements diverged from its books in every quarter of three years.

parameter_scores.basis: EBITDA margin 13.67% → 16.01% → 18.97% and PAT margin 8.02% → 10.43% → 12.10% across FY24–FY26 on revenue from operations of ₹ 4,460.84 / 5,079.12 / 5,340.25 mn; PAT ₹ 357.91 / 529.51 / 646.36 mn; EBITDA per ton ₹ 7,433.60 / 9,125.51 / 11,494.66 as printed. The RHP's own CAGRs for the span are 9.41% (revenue) and 34.38% (PAT). Margin gain came alongside a fall in material cost from 68.62% to 61.02% of total expenses.

Debt-to-equity 0.21 / 0.03 / 0.06 times and Debt/EBITDA 0.68 / 0.09 / 0.18 times across FY24–FY26; total borrowings ₹ 177.77 mn against net worth ₹ 3,060.99 mn at March 31, 2026; DSCR 5.27; finance cost ₹ 14.90 mn; ₹ 840.79 mn sanctioned against ₹ 148.65 mn outstanding at May 31, 2026; contingent liabilities ₹ 35.58 mn with capital commitments ₹ 19.29 mn separate; no EPCG export obligation. Offsetting: cash and cash equivalents of only ₹ 11.42 mn (bank deposits of ₹ 414.51 mn sit outside that line, largely margin money), the facilities rest on personal guarantees of four Promoters, and no dividend has been paid in the last 3 fiscals or the current one.

CFO ₹ 371.44 / 618.86 / 275.38 mn across FY24–FY26 — falling in the latest year despite higher PBT, on a ₹ (488.61) mn working-capital movement. Working capital days 98 → 104 → 132 on the RHP's own definition; inventory days 34 → 42 → 57; cash conversion cycle 89 → 72 → 93; inventories 23.80% → 27.40% → 28.38% of total assets; receivables past 90 days ₹ 58.55 → 46.91 → 167.55 mn against an expected-credit-loss allowance of ₹ 2.17 mn.

Revenue from operations grew at a printed 9.41% CAGR over FY24–FY26 to ₹ 5,340.25 mn, but sales volume was 82,042.18 / 89,103.48 / 88,152.20 MT — lower in FY26 than FY25 — so the latest year's growth is mix and realisation rather than tonnage. Within the RHP's own peer table the issuer is the second-smallest by total income (Steelcast ₹ 4,231.66 mn; Jayaswal Neco ₹ 71,318.20 mn; AIA Engineering ₹ 44,198.64 mn; RHI Magnesita ₹ 40,199.45 mn).

No customer above 10% of revenue from operations in any of the three fiscals; top customer 6.96%, top 5 25.49% and top 10 38.00% in FY26; 1,825 cumulative customers, 578 served during FY26, repeat-customer revenue ₹ 4,522.77 mn (84.69%). Offsetting within the same disclosure: churn of 38.58% in FY26 (from 34.73%), retention of 62.98%, and unique new customers of only 144 against 157 two years earlier.

The RHP states the Company enters into NO contract longer than one year with customers, and no long-term contract or arrangement with suppliers either — everything is purchase-order based. The Order Book of ₹ 1,785.69 mn (May 31, 2026) is described as firm purchase orders that 'is neither indicative of future growth nor is it a guarantee of future revenues' and may be cancelled, put in abeyance or delayed; no unexecuted/to-be-executed percentage is printed. Automobile revenue fell in absolute terms in each of the last two years.

Chartered-engineer-certified installed capacity 100,589 → 119,464 → 119,690 MT with utilisation 85.47% → 90.30% → 87.71%; the Rolling Mill Division being expanded fell to 82.02% from 88.24% on flat 65,000 MT capacity, while SMS and Foundry runs at 94.47%. The Net Proceeds capex leaves Facility 1's total installed capacity unchanged at 54,690 MT (rolls/castings +5,000 MT, ingots −5,000 MT) and adds 15,000 MT at Facility 2, with no statement anywhere that the addition is order-backed.

100% of the ₹ 630.39 mn capex rests on quotations: no purchase order placed, no payment made, no definitive agreement with any vendor, vendors only Board-approved on June 28, 2026, and nine quotations dated June 4–13, 2026 with 4-month validity lapse around early October 2026 — yet every quantified object is scheduled wholly within Fiscal 2027 with nil deployed. No appraisal by any agency, bank or financial institution; no monitoring agency because the Fresh Issue does not exceed ₹ 1,000 mn (Regulation 41 not triggered). The second object (repayment of ₹ 5.70 mn of HDFC working-capital term loans) is lender-identified with Nil prepayment penalty and auditor-certified past utilisation; general corporate purposes is printed [●], capped at 25% of Gross Proceeds.

parameter_scores.basis: Material divergences between the quarterly stock and book-debt statements filed with HDFC and ICICI and the books in every quarter of three years (up to ₹ 80.23 mn on debtors, ₹ 70.84 mn on inventories), with inventory not valued at all for three FY2026 quarters; the statutory auditor resigned mid-term on August 1, 2024 with no reason disclosed and the successor signed the FY2024 opinion seven weeks after appointment; no CARO 2020 annexure and no Rule 11(g) audit-trail reporting appears anywhere in the RHP; statutory-dues delays worsened into FY2026 (TDS 17 instances / 2,566 days). Offsetting: the examination report states there are no qualifications in any of the three years requiring restatement adjustment, and no emphasis of matter is printed.

10 directors, 5 independent, 1 woman; 4 directors plus the CEO, COO and CFO are one family and the CFO is the Chairman's grandson; all five committees constituted on February 25, 2025 with the same three Independent Directors on every one and two Independent Directors on none; the Managing Director sits on the Audit Committee and chairs the Risk Management Committee; 4 of 5 Independent Directors and every non-independent director have no listed-company board experience; not one director cessation is disclosed in three years. Offsetting: no wilful-defaulter, debarment, struck-off or SEBI-action disclosure against any Director or Promoter, and no change of control in five years.

Related-party transactions fell from ₹ 984.07 mn (22.06% of revenue, FY24) to ₹ 18.30 mn (0.34%, FY26) and family loans are fully unwound — but three Promoter Group entities remain in a similar line of business with two issuer directors on BLC Metals' board, no financials for the sole Group Company are printed in the RHP, the corporate office and all green-belt land are leased from promoter-family lessors on four arrangements all expiring January 31, 2027, one of those lessors is a Selling Shareholder, and ₹ 240.32 mn was routed to BLC Metals as a loan in FY2024 (repaid in-year with ₹ 4.98 mn interest) followed by ₹ 94.00 mn on preference-share redemption in FY2025.

Promoters 47.39% and Promoter Group a further 41.12%, together 88.51% pre-Offer, with the post-Offer column printed [●]; no shares pledged; Regulation 14/16 lock-in of 20% of post-Offer capital for 3 years with the excess for 1 year, and the entire remaining pre-Offer capital for 6 months under Regulation 17(1) — but the whole Promoters' contribution and lock-in table (Note 22.b) is printed [●], so no specific shares are yet identified as minimum promoters' contribution. Family sellers' auditor-certified average cost is ₹ 1.12–₹ 5.18 per ₹ 10 share; a 4:1 bonus created ~87% of the pre-Offer count 15 months before the RHP; no ESOP scheme exists and no employee reservation is offered.

parameter_scores.basis: Cost of materials consumed 61.02% of total expenses in FY26 (scrap alone 46.10%), bought on purchase orders with no long-term supplier contracts; top-10 suppliers 38.39% of total expenses and 49.00% of total purchases; power and fuel a further 7.64% and rising faster than revenue; the RHP states margins suffer to the extent price escalation cannot be passed on and that price falls in downturns 'have not always been balanced by proportional price increases during periods of economic recovery'. Foreign-currency exposure of EUR 0.64 mn and USD 0.04 mn is wholly unhedged.

THE PRICE BAND IS NOT IN THIS DOCUMENT. The Offer Price, Floor and Cap Price, the number of Fresh Issue shares, the total Offer size, the OFS rupee value, post-Offer capital and shareholding, Net Proceeds, general corporate purposes, every offer-expense line, dilution, the 'Cap Price is X times WACA' multiple and every P/E and NAV-at-price figure are printed [●]; the peer table prints the issuer's own P/E and EV/EBITDA as 'NA'. No valuation, market capitalisation or price-based comparison can be stated from this document and none has been formed here. The peer table also mixes standalone and consolidated bases and face values of ₹ 1, ₹ 2 and ₹ 10, and prints no average or median row.

red_flags: Material divergences between the quarterly stock and book-debt statements filed with HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank for drawing-power purposes and the books of account, in EVERY quarter of all three fiscals — up to ₹ 80.23 million on book debts (June 2024) and ₹ 70.84 million on inventories (March 2026) — with inventory not valued at all for the quarters ended June, September and December 2025.

ZERO committed deployment for the ₹ 630.39 million capex: no purchase order placed, no payment made and 'no definitive agreements with any of these vendors', with vendors approved only on June 28, 2026 and nine quotations lapsing around early October 2026, against a schedule that puts 100% of every quantified object in Fiscal 2027.

No monitoring agency (the Fresh Issue of ₹ 930.00 mn does not cross the ₹ 1,000 mn Regulation 41 threshold) and no appraisal of the Objects by any agency, bank or financial institution — while the Audit Committee that receives the quarterly utilisation disclosure has the Managing Director as a member.

The statutory auditor resigned mid-term on August 1, 2024 with NO reason disclosed anywhere in the RHP; the successor firm, appointed the same day to fill the casual vacancy, signed the Fiscal 2024 audit report seven weeks later and now certifies all three restated years.

No CARO 2020 annexure and no Rule 11(g) audit-trail reporting is reproduced anywhere in the RHP — an absence of disclosure, not a clean opinion; nothing can be read either way about adverse remarks on inventory, statutory dues or the accounting-software audit trail.

The larger part of the capex produces no net capacity: Manufacturing Facility 1's total installed capacity stays at 54,690 MT (metal rolls and engineering castings +5,000 MT offset by ingots −5,000 MT), while Facility 2's 15,000 MT addition is nowhere stated to be supported by orders — in a business that signs no contract longer than one year.

Rolling Mill utilisation FELL to 82.02% from 88.24% on capacity unchanged at 65,000 MT, and aggregate utilisation fell to 87.71% from 90.30%, immediately before an Offer whose stated purpose is to add capacity.

Working capital days rose to 132 from 98 in two years and operating cash flow fell to ₹ 275.38 mn from ₹ 618.86 mn on a ₹ (488.61) mn working-capital build, while receivables past 90 days tripled to ₹ 167.55 million and cash and cash equivalents stood at ₹ 11.42 million.

Statutory-dues delays worsened in the pre-IPO year: TDS 17 instances and 2,566 aggregate days in Fiscal 2026 against 15 instances and 2,010 days in Fiscal 2025 and nil in Fiscal 2024, plus a first GST delay of 337 days.

Four of ten directors plus the CEO, COO and CFO are one family, the CFO is the Chairman's grandson, the Managing Director sits on the Audit Committee and chairs the Risk Management Committee, all five committees were constituted on a single day (February 25, 2025) and the two most experienced Independent Directors sit on none of them.

Three RoC filings carry incorrect information — including Form 32 recording the founder-Managing Director's category as 'Independent' and a directorship term ending on the non-existent date 'February 30, 2030' — alongside untraceable education documents for the Chairman and Vice Chairman and an outside practising Company Secretary certifying 'certain untraceable corporate records' that the RHP never lists.

The corporate office and all three green-belt land parcels are leased from promoter-family members on four arrangements all expiring January 31, 2027, one of the lessors (Yogita Garg) is offering up to 2,143,623 shares in this Offer, and the RHP still asserts there is no lessor conflict of interest.

Three Promoter Group entities are in a similar line of business with two serving issuer directors on BLC Metals' board, while the same paragraph asserts the Promoters have no interest in any similar venture and states only that conflict procedures will be adopted 'as and when' a conflict arises; no financials for the sole Group Company are printed in the RHP.

Risk Factor 20 states 'Our Company, and Promoters, are currently not involved in any legal proceedings' and then tables ₹ 8.21 million of tax proceedings against the Company and ₹ 0.85 million against the Promoters — an internal contradiction on the face of the document.

The credit rating changed both agency and grade (CRISIL BBB+/A2 to CARE A-/A2+, assigned August 3, 2026, three days before this RHP) while the document describes the rating as having 'remained consistent in the preceding 3 financial years'.
strengths_observed: Profitable in all three restated years with margins widening in each of them, on the RHP's own printed figures: revenue from operations ₹ 4,460.84 mn (FY24), ₹ 5,079.12 mn (FY25), ₹ 5,340.25 mn (FY26); EBITDA ₹ 609.86 / 813.12 / 1,013.28 mn at EBITDA margins of 13.67% / 16.01% / 18.97%; PAT ₹ 357.91 / 529.51 / 646.36 mn at PAT margins of 8.02% / 10.43% / 12.10%; basic and diluted EPS ₹ 10.07 / 13.56 / 16.56 (bonus-adjusted). The RHP prints its own CAGRs for the FY24–FY26 span: revenue from operations 9.41% and profit after tax 34.38%. Fiscal columns are printed newest-first and were read in that order.

The balance sheet carries very little debt and the RHP's own ratio table shows it: total borrowings ₹ 412.13 mn (FY24), ₹ 75.77 mn (FY25), ₹ 177.77 mn (FY26) against net worth of ₹ 1,936.59 / 2,416.16 / 3,060.99 mn; debt-to-equity 0.21 / 0.03 / 0.06 times; Debt/EBITDA 0.68 / 0.09 / 0.18 times; debt service coverage ratio 1.08 / 9.13 / 5.27; finance cost only ₹ 23.09 / 13.58 / 14.90 mn. As at May 31, 2026 total sanctioned facilities were ₹ 840.79 mn against ₹ 148.65 mn outstanding, and the FY2024 unsecured family/shareholder loans of ₹ 329.81 mn have been fully repaid.

Return ratios are in the high teens to high twenties throughout, taken verbatim from the auditor-certified KPI table: ROE 22.83% / 24.31% / 23.60%, ROCE 21.98% / 28.24% / 27.11% and RoNW 18.48% / 21.92% / 21.12% for FY24 / FY25 / FY26, with a printed weighted-average RoNW of 20.94% and NAV per Equity Share of ₹ 54.47 / ₹ 61.89 / ₹ 78.41.

Customer concentration is genuinely low and the RHP states it plainly: none of the top 10 customers individually contributed 10% of revenue from operations in any of the three fiscals. Top customer 7.85% / 8.38% / 6.96% (₹ 350.25 / 425.94 / 371.68 mn), top 5 27.86% / 27.82% / 25.49% and top 10 37.81% / 39.91% / 38.00% (₹ 1,686.51 / 2,027.16 / 2,029.21 mn) for FY24 / FY25 / FY26. Cumulative customers served reached 1,825 by FY26 (1,681 and 1,544 earlier), 578 served during FY26, and revenue from repeat customers was ₹ 4,522.77 mn or 84.69% of revenue from operations, with the FY26 top-10 averaging a 6-year relationship.

Both operating plants are owned freehold on non-agricultural land with duly stamped and registered deeds (8 acres at Village Salani, 10 acres at Village Turan, ~790,000 sq ft combined), the capex to be funded from the Net Proceeds is brownfield expansion at those same owned sites with no land to be acquired, and the RHP states statutory and environmental approvals for the equipment/machinery and rooftop solar at both facilities have already been obtained. Installed capacity of 119,690 MT and every utilisation figure are certified by GATS India Ltd, an independent chartered engineer, per certificate dated August 6, 2026.

Related-party dealing has collapsed to near-nil ahead of the Offer: the sum of all related party transactions was ₹ 984.07 mn (22.06% of revenue from operations) in FY2024, ₹ 490.31 mn (9.65%) in FY2025 and ₹ 18.30 mn (0.34%) in FY2026. Loans taken from related parties fell from ₹ 218.51 mn to ₹ 1.81 mn to nil, and loans outstanding to related parties were ₹ 329.80 mn at March 31, 2024 and nil thereafter. No interest was paid to or received from any promoter-group party in FY2026 or FY2025.

None of the Equity Shares held by the Promoters, and none of the shares offered in the Offer for Sale, are pledged or otherwise encumbered as on the date of the RHP; the RHP separately states no shares held by any Shareholder are pledged.

Disclosed litigation quantum is small and every non-tax head is nil: against the Company 4 tax proceedings aggregating ₹ 8.21 million (1 direct tax ₹ 0.17 mn, 3 indirect tax ₹ 8.04 mn) and against the Promoters 2 direct-tax matters aggregating ₹ 0.85 million, with criminal proceedings, statutory/regulatory actions, SEBI or exchange disciplinary action and material civil litigation all Nil for the Company, Promoters, Directors, KMP and Senior Management. These per-entity aggregates are not added together here.

Off-balance-sheet exposure is limited and disclosed cleanly: contingent liabilities of ₹ 35.58 million at March 31, 2026 (bank guarantees in favour of others ₹ 28.43 mn plus Others ₹ 7.15 mn) against net worth of ₹ 3,060.99 million, with capital commitments of ₹ 19.29 million disclosed as a separate line and not folded in. The RHP states expressly that the Company never applied for the EPCG scheme, on commercial-viability grounds, so no export obligation is outstanding against its export base; it uses duty drawback only.

The Order Book has risen across all three year-ends and again since: ₹ 855.45 mn (March 31, 2024), ₹ 930.03 mn (March 31, 2025), ₹ 1,182.87 mn (March 31, 2026) and ₹ 1,785.69 mn as on May 31, 2026 — read against the caveat below that the Company signs no customer contract longer than one year.

Eligibility is via the profitability route under Regulation 6(1), on figures printed in the RHP: operating profit ₹ 483.54 / 623.34 / 755.80 mn for FY24 / FY25 / FY26 with an average of ₹ 620.89 mn; net worth ₹ 1,936.59 / 2,416.16 / 3,060.99 mn; net tangible assets ₹ 1,937.27 / 2,414.06 / 3,058.22 mn; monetary assets 20.18% / 15.92% / 17.40% of net tangible assets.

End-market mix broadened materially over the period even as the largest segment shrank: Engineering – Industrial Equipment went from ₹ 209.81 mn (4.71%) in FY24 to ₹ 899.96 mn (16.85%) in FY26, Others (aerospace and defence, cement, thermal power) from ₹ 116.17 mn to ₹ 291.79 mn, and overseas revenue from ₹ 215.67 mn (4.83%) to ₹ 479.78 mn (8.98%), across 21 countries and 5 continents with One Star Export House recognition.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward and forward integration within a single site cluster: the Company describes itself as an integrated iron and steel manufacturing company operating two integrated divisions - a Steel Melting Shop (SMS) and Foundry Division and a Rolling Mill Division. The SMS runs 12 MT fully digital medium-frequency induction furnaces in twin-shell configuration with secondary metallurgy via ladle refining furnace (LRF) and vacuum degassing (VD); the foundry has an in-house engineering and pattern development unit, continuous sand mixers, mechanised fettling via automatic shakeout, a sand reclamation plant, shot blasting and automatic paint booths; downstream are heat treatment furnaces, machine shops (>100,000 sq ft covered, CNC lathes, boring machines, roll grinding, VTL/CNC VTL, plano and CNC vertical milling) and rolling mills. Manufacturing and machining processes are described as overlapping and fungible, so the available (installed) capacity of the SMS and Foundry Division can vary with the product mix being run. Upstream, raw material (scrap, ingots, ferro alloys) is procured directly from domestic manufacturers and international suppliers without middlemen, on purchase orders rather than long term contracts; internally generated scrap is re-melted and recycled. Downstream, the Company sells directly through its in-house sales team, keeping middle-men and agents out of the sales process because products are highly customised and engineered; orders are purchase-order based with customer projections used for production planning, and long term contracts are generally avoided due to steel price volatility. Utilities: a 66 KvA sub-station, grid power from the Punjab State Electricity Board, ground water, and around 2 MW of installed rooftop solar. Corporate structure was consolidated through a Scheme of Amalgamation (NCLT Chandigarh order dated August 22, 2024) merging Belco Special Steels Private Limited (now the Rolling Mill Division) and Parkash Multimetals Private Limited (now part of the SMS and Foundry Division) into the Company.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Revenue from the top 10 customers was Rs 2,029.21 million, Rs 2,027.16 million and Rs 1,686.51 million (38.00%, 39.91% and 37.81% of revenue from operations) in Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024, with the largest single customer at 6.96% in Fiscal 2026. The Company does not enter into long term contracts and its business is based on purchase orders, so demand can fall away at short notice.
- Cost of material consumed - primarily scrap and ferro alloys sourced domestically and internationally - was 61.02%, 60.78% and 68.62% of total expenses in Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024. There are no long-term supply agreements with third party suppliers, and steel pricing is subject to market demand, volatility and economic conditions.
- Net working capital was Rs 1,924.50 million as at March 31, 2026 (132 working capital days) versus Rs 1,453.68 million (104 days) at March 31, 2025 and Rs 1,196.40 million (98 days) at March 31, 2024, with inventory days rising from 34 to 42 to 57. Sanctioned working capital facilities were Rs 691.03 million as on May 31, 2026 with Rs 94.36 million outstanding.
- Alloy steel products, metal rolls and engineering castings cumulatively contributed more than 90.00% of revenue from operations in each of Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024 (91.70%, 93.14% and 94.29% from sale of customised products), so a downturn in any one of these segments is material.
- All manufacturing operations - and the Upcoming Manufacturing Facility - are located in Mandi Gobindgarh, Punjab, exposing the Company to concentrated regional, regulatory, labour and natural-event risk.
- Sales to customers in India were Rs 4,860.47 million, Rs 4,859.33 million and Rs 4,245.17 million (91.02%, 95.67% and 95.17% of revenue from operations) in Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024. Domestic sub-total was essentially flat between Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2026; growth came from exports.
- Construction of the Upcoming Manufacturing Facility has only recently commenced and its completion and operation are contingent on obtaining various approvals; delays could cause cost and time overruns. The Company has not yet placed orders for the capital expenditure equipment and machinery to be funded from the Net Proceeds, and the fund requirements have not been appraised by any bank or financial institution.
- The Order Book was Rs 1,182.87 million as on March 31, 2026 (Rs 930.03 million and Rs 855.45 million at the two prior year ends) and Rs 1,785.69 million as of May 31, 2026, but the Company states that current order book value is not necessarily indicative of future growth and some orders may be modified or cancelled.
